passage: The mock paper lay folded in Hana's schoolbag for two nights, a red mark at the top low enough to hurt. Hana's father, Anders, had cut back on holidays to pay for the evening tutor, and every time he asked "How is it going?" Hana's throat closed. On the third evening Hana laid the paper on the kitchen table in Gothenburg. "Pappa, I have to show you something." Anders read it in silence. "I'm scared," Hana said. "You've spent so much on the tutor. I can try harder, but I can't carry all of it. If I fail, I need you still on my side." Anders took off his glasses. "I didn't know it felt that heavy," he said. "Let's make a plan, together."

qa.q: For how long was the mock paper hidden in Hana's schoolbag?
qa.a: The mock paper lay folded in Hana's schoolbag for two nights.

qa.q: What was Hana afraid of when thinking about the result?
qa.a: Hana was afraid of letting down Anders after he spent so much on the tutor, and of losing his support if Hana failed.

qa.q: What might have gone wrong if Hana had kept hiding the mock paper?
qa.a: The fear would probably have grown, and the secret could have exploded later at a worse moment, for both Hana and Anders.

qa.q: What was Anders thinking as he took off his glasses?
qa.a: Anders seemed surprised and sorry, realising his hopes felt "that heavy" to Hana, and wanted to help with a plan.

grounding: Hana dreads the result because the parent has spent savings, and tells the father plainly how much can be carried instead of hiding the mock score.

passage:
The practice board result came out on Wednesday: 58 per cent. Salma folded the sheet into four and slid it under her geometry box.

At home in their Bhopal flat, Ammi was on the phone with an aunt. "Coaching fees, extra tuition, everything. We've put what we saved into this year. She'll do us proud." Salma heard it from the corridor and felt her throat close.

For two days she said the results weren't out. Her friend Damini found her crying in the library on Friday. "You can't keep hiding it. When the real result comes, it'll be ten times worse."

That evening Salma sat down with both her parents. She put the sheet on the table. "58. I'm sorry I hid it. I'm scared all the time because I know how much you've put into this. I'll work, I promise. But I can't carry everything you're hoping for. I need you to know that."

Abbu looked at the sheet a long time. Then he pushed his tea towards her. "Talk. Tell us what's heavy."

qa.q: What percentage did Salma get in the practice board result?
What was Salma feeling when she heard Ammi on the phone?
qa.a: Salma felt dread and pressure, her throat closing, because her parents had put what they saved into this year and expected her to make them proud.

qa.q: What went wrong at first, and what fixed it?
qa.a: Hiding the result for two days made Salma more anxious; telling both parents plainly and saying how much she could carry fixed it.

qa.q: How might Abbu feel when Salma says she can't carry everything?
qa.a: Abbu may feel worried and a little guilty, but he chooses to listen, pushing his tea towards her and asking what is heavy.

grounding: It shows a teen dreading results because parents have staked hopes and savings on them, who stops hiding a bad mock score and tells them plainly how much she can carry.

passage:
"Yusuf, your mock marks came?" Abba asked at dinner.

"Yes." Yusuf put his spoon down. "Can I say something first?"

Zubin, his elder brother, glanced over. Ammi stopped serving.

"You've spent so much on my coaching. Zubin bhai even gave up his bike money. Every day I hear 'this is our hope.' I dream about the result. I wake up at three with my heart going."

"Beta—" Ammi began.

"I got 61 in the mock. I didn't want to tell you. But if I hide it and the board result is bad, it'll be worse." He breathed out. "I'll give everything I can. But I can't promise a rank. I need you to hear that."

Abba was quiet. Zubin put a hand on his shoulder. "Abba, I felt the same in my year. I never said it."

Abba looked at both his sons. "Then we talk every Sunday. Not about ranks. About how you are."

qa.q: What mark did Yusuf get in the mock?
What was Yusuf feeling in the weeks before the dinner?
qa.a: Yusuf felt anxious and under pressure, dreaming about the result and waking at three with his heart racing.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Yusuf to tell his family before the board result?
qa.a: Telling them now, with his fear and his limits, avoided a bigger explosion later and let his family respond with support.

qa.q: How does Zubin see what Yusuf is going through?
qa.a: Zubin understands it from his own year and feels moved to admit he felt the same but never said it.

grounding: It shows a teen dreading his board result because his family has staked hopes and savings on it, telling them plainly how much he can carry instead of hiding a mock score.
